checks.claim: The original model is kept in full: every H:homog Gamma, d=1,2,3, 0<a<1, 0<alpha<d or alpha=d=1, alpha+a<2, the zero covariance, a single physical mask m_R=eta_root(x/R)^2, and both displacement and fast velocity.
checks.reason: Target lines 8-13 match the U, SP, C3 and BT notes. The exponent window is nonempty: 1-a/2>1/2 because a<1, and (3-a-alpha)/2>1/2 because alpha+a<2. Also r>1/(1-theta)>2 and r<2/a, and the d=1 white-noise case (alpha=d=1) is admissible. With Gamma=0, H_sp={0}, the class reduces to {0}, Rate=0 and Pmean_m=S_E(ell_m); US3a/b still hold because log||S_E(B)||/B <= log(3B)/B -> 0.

checks.claim: US1 closure: every element of Vclass_E,R determines a unique real V in H^-1/2 supported in supp m_R. This uses a fixed-R cutoff chi_R and needs no F constant column.
checks.reason: With chi_R=1 near supp m_R, M_{V_n}chi_R=V_n. So ||V_n-V_m||_{H^-1/2} <= ||chi_R||_{H^1/2}||M_n-M_m||, with an R-dependent constant used only to identify V. The support is closed under limits, and multiplication by a smooth compact u is bounded on H^-1/2, so M u=Vu on tests; density gives uniqueness. The same bound makes the F norm of L_n-L_m at most (1+||chi_R||_{H^1/2})||M_n-M_m||, so a fixed-R lift into the accepted F class mathcalV_R exists. That lift is used only to identify the actual flow, as the target states.

checks.claim: US1 form, domain and dual statements hold with E-only K>=max(1,||M_V||): A>=1, D(A^1/2)=H1, D(A^1/4)=H^1/2, negative dual equal to H^-1/2, and .5||u||_H1^2 <= q_V+c||u||^2 <= 3(1+K^2)||u||_H1^2.
checks.reason: Recomputed independently. |<Vu,u>| <= k||u||_{1/2}^2 <= K b z with b=||u||_2, z=||u||_H1, by Fourier Cauchy-Schwarz. AM-GM gives q+c b^2 >= z^2/2+(1+K^2/2)b^2 >= .5 z^2 and >=2b^2, and the upper bound is <= 3(1+K^2)z^2. Only the dual-pairing bound (S1 eq. 6) is used, which needs only the E norm of M_V; the F constant column enters nowhere. The quarter-power identification comes from the accepted own operator-monotonicity argument (S1 Section 3, constants 2^-1/4 and L_K^1/4); no KLMN, Heinz or rough H2 domain is imported. Complexification preserves norms.

checks.claim: US1a: beta(V)=inf spec H_V, -K^2<=beta<=0, lambda<=K, and ||P_V(t)||_B(E) <= 8(1+K)^2(1+t)exp(lambda t) holds with the E norm K alone.
checks.reason: Recomputed the entries of the spectral matrix (11). For h>=0: sqrt(h+c)|S_t| <= 1+sqrt(c)t and |hS_t|/sqrt(h+c) <= 1. For beta<=h<0: sqrt(|h|)sinh/sqrt(h+c) <= K e^{lambda t} and sqrt(c)t e^{lambda t}. With sqrt(c)<=2K for K>=1, each entry is <= 2(1+K)(1+t)e^{lambda t}, the block norm is <= 2b, and the condition-number factor is M_K^2=sqrt(3(1+K^2)) <= 2(1+K); the product is 8(1+K)^2. A finer estimate gives about 3.2(1+K)^1.5, so the constant is valid and not tight. beta<=0 follows from dilated bumps translated outside the compact supp m_R. The lower bound -K^2 follows from z^2-1-Kz >= -(1+K^2)/2. No gap, positivity or division by lambda is needed. The identity with the actual E Young flow is S2 Section 5's E-only Duhamel/core argument, using compact L_E and a Lipschitz primitive; this is a proof obligation, not something proved in the packet.

checks.claim: US1b: the beta and lambda continuity constants (K+2) and sqrt((K+2)d0) hold in the E operator norm.
checks.reason: ||B_E(V)-B_E(W)||_B(E)=||M_V-M_W|| exactly. An eta-minimizer for W has z<=K+2 because z^2-Kz-2<=0, and |q_V-q_W| <= d0 z. The square-root step uses |sqrt x - sqrt y| <= sqrt|x-y|. Only E norms enter.

checks.claim: Teschl is the 2014 SECOND edition (GSM 157), and the imported theorems are pinpointed with checkable hypotheses.
checks.reason: The images confirm the SECOND EDITION title, ISBN 978-1-4704-1704-8 and the 2009/2014 copyright. Printed p80 defines hermitian, semi-bounded and closed forms. On p81, Thm 2.14/(2.63) requires a densely defined, closed, semi-bounded hermitian form; q_V on Q=H1 is real-valued and semi-bounded, and its q-norm is equivalent to the complete H1 norm, so Q=H_q. On p102, Thm 3.1 is the bounded Borel calculus with strong convergence. Printed p103 (text only, (3.26)-(3.28)) gives D_f and the cutoffs. On p104, Thm 3.2 covers (3.29)-(3.33). On p109, Thm 3.6 gives (3.51)-(3.53), with form domain Q(A)=D(|A|^1/2). None of these is used to assert H2, a gap or positivity.

checks.claim: US2: Bochner averaging over true cells gives sup_{R>=1,||Phi||<=M}||barW-W||_Lr <= M_0 M omega_delta -> 0, with no spatial compactness.
checks.reason: A_delta is a contraction on scalar L^r (Jensen; each nonempty cell is averaged over its own length) and converges strongly to I as the mesh delta*B -> 0. It is uniformly bounded by 2, and C_t:H_t->L^r is compact for r<2/a, so omega_delta=||(A_delta-I)C_t|| -> 0. Bochner integrals commute with the bounded pointwise T_R. On finite tensors A_delta^(H_sp)(C_t ⊗ I) = (A_delta C_t) ⊗ I, which extends by density. U (15) gives the dimension-free Hilbert-valued bound for r>=2 (Gaussian convexity argument), and U (6) gives M_0 independent of R. The infinite orthonormal spatial sequence in U Section 5 shows no tensor compactness is claimed. Averages stay in the closed linear class.

checks.claim: US2 integrated-rate bound: integral of |lambda(barW)-lambda(W)| <= sqrt(3+2 C_mean M) sqrt(M_0 M omega_delta).
checks.reason: Apply US1b pointwise with K(s)=max(1,||W||,||barW||), then Cauchy-Schwarz. The L1 norms are <= the L^r norms on I=(0,1). Jensen gives ||barW||_L1 <= ||W||_L1 <= C_mean M with C_mean=M_0||C_t|| from U (17). Rate is finite, nonnegative and continuous because lambda <= max(1,||W||).

checks.claim: US3 budgets on E: G_B<=3B, C_B<=18B^(3-1/r)<=32B^(3-1/r), C_B B^(1/r)>=B, and the generic Young bound log||S_E U_D|| <= C_theta B(1+||D||^nu).
checks.reason: The Frobenius norm of the Bessel-unitary free matrix is sqrt(3+2B^2) <= 3B. Since B^(1-1/r-theta) <= B^(1-1/r), C_B <= 18B^(3-1/r). G_B>=1 gives C_B B^(1/r)>=B. The primitive bound ||H_m||_theta <= C_B delta^(-1/r)||W||_Lr(I_m) uses theta<1-1/r, which follows from r>1/(1-theta). B1's C_theta=4+log4+2(4c_theta)^nu covers log G_B <= log(4B); the Young constants are dimension-free because multiplication on B(E) has norm 1.

checks.claim: US3a: the good/bad/true-partial/empty decomposition, the signs, and the RHS L_BK/B + C_theta 32^r Z^r B^(3r)(K^-r+K^(nu-r)) are correct and uniform over R>=1.
checks.reason: Rederived from B2. Good full cells (a_m<=K) have ||barM_m|| <= a_m/B <= K. E1 is applied with left endpoint S_E(B) and constant C(theta,B,K), uniform in R. The static US1 bound (16-power version) gives prefactors summing to <= L_BK/B, because delta*N <= 1/B and good cells are full. Rates satisfy delta*sum B lambda(barM_m) <= integral of lambda(barW) <= Rate + Lambda_delta, and dropping bad, last and empty cells is valid because lambda>=0. On bad cells, 1+a_m^nu <= (K^-r+K^(nu-r))a_m^r and delta*sum a_m^r <= C_B^r Z^r give C_theta B C_B^r Z^r(...) <= C_theta 32^r B^(3r)Z^r(...). The partial last cell contributes C_theta B[delta + C_B^nu Z^nu delta^(1-nu/r)] -> 0 since nu<r; the empty cell is I. Omega_delta and Lambda_delta are uniform in R by US2.

checks.claim: US3/US4: the SP pure-mean baseline ||Pmean_m||>=1 holds at every R, delta, B and Phi, including true partial and empty cells, without bounded fast raw costs.
checks.reason: SP4 (23) is a qualitative symplectic identity: P^*J_E P=J_E with ||J_E||=1. The fast direction phi_m=delta^(-a/2)T_m^*Phi is finite at each delta and is used only to identify the driver; no uniform bound is needed. SP4 holds for any fixed R>0, any Phi in H_I, the stopped partial cell, and ell_m=0 (where the block is I). U states that its T_R∘U agrees with the E restriction of the completed physical mean, i.e. SP's i^*T_F i. The US proof must cite this explicitly (minor).

checks.claim: US3b: with M_B=M0 B^m and K_B=B^s, s>r(3+m)/(r-nu), the iterated limit is <=0, with delta first at each fixed B and no diagonal limit.
checks.reason: The exponent r(3+m)+s(nu-r) is <0 by the strict condition. Since r/(r-nu)>1, s>3+m and so r(3+m)-sr<0. The term [log16+4log(1+B^s)+3log(1+B)]/B tends to 0. M_B is fixed before the inner delta limit. The scalar product of block norms is not equated with the norm of the ordered product.

checks.claim: US4a: for an arbitrary non-Hamiltonian residual on the full tuple domain, delta log max(1,z) <= C_Kres[(2/B)^(1-1/p)Y+(2/B)^(1-nu/p)Y^nu] + c_B D_M(Kres^-r+Kres^(nu-r)).
checks.reason: E1 holds for every zero-started C^theta perturbation in any Banach phase, with no x=0 penalty and any left multiplier, so it applies on B(E). Good cells (a_m<=Kres) give log ratio <= C(theta,B,Kres)(v_m+v_m^nu). On bad cells, ||Pmean_m||>=1 (SP) lets the ratio be bounded by ||Ppert_m||, then by c_B(1+a_m^nu+v_m^nu) with c_B independent of Kres. Finite Hölder with exponents p>=1 and p/nu>=1 gives delta*sum v_m <= (delta n)^(1-1/p)Y and delta*sum v_m^nu <= (delta n)^(1-nu/p)Y^nu, with delta n<=2/B. D_M=C_B^r(C_mean M)^r is uniform in R. Positivity follows from invertible Young and free evolutions. No residual symplecticity, Gaussianity or independence is used.

checks.claim: US4b: the max(1,·)/product step and the order delta -> Kres -> B are correct.
checks.reason: ||ordered product|| <= z·product of ||Pmean_m||, and the product of mean norms is >=1. Hence log max(1,ab) <= log max(1,a)+log b for b>=1, so F - 2·delta·sum log||Pmean|| <= 2·delta·log max(1,z). On Y<=b_delta with b_delta->0, the limsup over delta is <= 2c_B D_{M_B}(Kres^-r+Kres^(nu-r)) for every Kres, hence <=0. Adding US3b (limsup of a sum <= sum of limsups) gives (US4b).

minor: Notation clash: 'M0' in US3b (M_B=M0 B^m, any M0>0) collides with M_0=||J_R|| bound in the mean definition, and the exponent 'm' collides with the block index m in sum_m. Rename (e.g. M_B=c_0 B^kappa) in the proof to avoid tying the radius scale to the J_R constant.
US2 writes 'Lr' without saying L^r(I;B(E)), or K(E), operator-norm valued; state it, plus strong measurability of W_R,Phi in the separable closed span.

US3/US4 rely on SP4, which is stated for SP's compression i^* mathcalT_F i, while the US mean is U's T_R∘(C_t⊗I). The proof should cite U Sections 2 and 6 for the equality of these two E means at every R>=1, and recheck that SP's mask eta(x/R)^2 equals the U and B mask.

The E-only Young=ordinary=spectral identification for elements of Vclass_E,R (compact L_E, Lipschitz primitive, S2 Section 5 E-part) must be written as a fixed-R application. The fixed-R F lift constant (1+||chi_R||_{H^1/2}) must be shown to enter only identification, never US1a/b or the US3/US4 budgets.
The proof needs the explicit identity A_delta^{(B(E))}∘T_R∘U = T_R∘((A_delta C_t)⊗I) on the completed H_I, plus the definition of A_delta on the measure-zero empty last cell.

Write the remaining proof obligations in full: (i) E versions of the B1 constants and of E1/E2 with the SP denominator; (ii) uniformity in R of Omega_delta, Lambda_delta, D_M and C_E1; (iii) deterministic-sup continuity/Borel statements as in B2 Section 5; (iv) the true partial-cell delta^(1-nu/r) term and empty-cell factor 1.
